implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines (not the Kotlin stdlib) supplies the aggregation: coroutineScope { vendors.map { async(Dispatchers.IO) { ask(it) } }.awaitAll() } fans out and awaitAll suspends until every Deferred has completed, returning results in input order; structured concurrency then guarantees cancellation - a failure in one child cancels the scope and its siblings. For push-style message arrival, a Channel or Flow replaces the fan-out (chunked/fold while the completeness condition holds), and withTimeout supplies the time-out strategy that awaitAll itself does not have.
pitfalls: async inside coroutineScope with awaitAll propagates the first failure and cancels the rest; supervisorScope or per-async runCatching is required when partial results must survive a failure.
awaitAll has no deadline: combine with withTimeout, or a lost partial suspends the aggregate forever and leaks the scope.
Blocking calls (JDBC, file I/O) inside a coroutine stall the whole dispatcher - move them to Dispatchers.IO; GlobalScope async additionally escapes structured concurrency and leaks.
